target_customer: Consumers who want to cut back on or quit alcohol, paying for a premium subscription
problem: People who drink more than they want to find abstinence programs stigmatizing and have few evidence based, flexible tools for moderation.
business_model: Consumer subscription app with premium coaching, plus a non alcoholic drink product
product_category: Digital health app for alcohol reduction

competitors.name: Sunnyside
competitors.traction_then: claims 200,000 users by one source, launched 2020 and rebranded 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app with content, tracking and community; complexity is in behavioral content, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Community and content library help, but apps are copyable; scale of users and reviews give modest advantage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; competitors remained other startups and charities.

market_need_then: Pandemic era drinking increases and the sober curious trend created demand; founders interviewed over 500 users and in mid 2021 moved from quitting to cutting back.

branding.domain_note: Uses joinreframeapp.com rather than a bare .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Encouraging and non stigmatizing; taglines Drink Less, Live More and We do science, not stigma

branding.community_and_virality: Claims a 24/7 private community and over 23,000 five star reviews; covered by Fortune, TechCrunch, Atlanta Magazine and InsideHook.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong app store presence and multiple press features and a consistent no stigma message, but no evidence of iconic status.

pivots.why: Interviews showed many users wanted moderation, per a founder interview summary

outcome_analysis: Reframe grew from a Georgia Tech program project into a consumer app with reported millions of downloads. It raised a 1.4M seed in March 2021 and a 12.5M Series A in late 2021 at a reported 100M valuation. Positioning on moderation without stigma and strong ratings drove growth, and it later added a non alcoholic drink. It remains active.
notes: Series B of 17.4M in January 2022 led by Goodwater is reported by one source and FundedIQ only; unverified and not recorded as a round. Total raised estimates range from 14M to over 27M. Post money of 100M comes from a TechCrunch snippet via search and Fortune confirms the 12.5M amount. Founder education stated only as Georgia Tech graduates. Competitor dates are approximate; Sunnyside launch 2020 or 2021 per sources. Try Dry omitted as undated.
